concept: A lens makes an image where the bent rays from an object meet again.
goal: Discover that moving the object closer to the lens pushes the image away and makes it bigger.
phenomenon: An object arrow stands on a line to the left of a thin lens. Rays from its tip bend through the lens and meet on the right, where the inverted image forms.

interactions.target: left or right along the line through the lens
interactions.response: the rays redraw and the image slides and changes size

interactions.target: up or down to make it fatter or thinner
interactions.response: the rays bend more or less and the image moves

scene.apparatus: a thin lens on a long line, with an object arrow on the left and its image on the right
fills: labels for object, lens and image
scene.wideScreen: The line runs the full width of the bench, so a wide screen shows the object and image far apart.

motion: The rays and the image move as the object is dragged. Under reduced motion they jump to their new places.
science: 1 / v = 1 / f - 1 / u, so v = u f / (u - f)

expectedBehaviour.text: the image distance falls as the object moves away
the image is never bigger than the object over this range

predict.question: As the object comes closer to the lens, will its image get bigger or smaller?
predict.check: Drag the object slowly toward the lens and watch the image on the right.

steps: Drag the object far from the lens and read the image distance.
Drag it closer and watch the image move away and grow.
Drag the lens to make it fatter and see how the image moves.
